text: In investing, you get what you don't pay for. High management fees, trading costs, and taxes severely eat into the compounding returns of an investor over a long time horizon.
source: John Bogle — The Little Book of Common Sense Investing
author: John Bogle

text: Don't look for the needle in the haystack; just buy the haystack. Broad-market passive index funds will consistently outperform the vast majority of active managers over the long term due to lower costs and broader exposure.
source: John Bogle — The Little Book of Common Sense Investing
author: John Bogle

text: Reversion to the mean is the iron rule of the financial markets. The high-flying mutual funds of yesterday invariably crash back to earth, and the forgotten sectors eventually rise again.
source: John Bogle — The Little Book of Common Sense Investing
author: John Bogle

text: The greatest enemy of a good plan is the dream of a perfect plan. Stick to the good plan. Time is your friend; impulse is your enemy. Stay the course through market turbulence.
source: John Bogle — The Little Book of Common Sense Investing
author: John Bogle
